description:
Milestone 1:

Tools:
Dev Tool: NRF52832 (NRF52-DK)
Software: Using Zephyr & NRF Connect SDK 2.3, VS Code
Dev board 1: Ideally you have PAC1954 https://www.mikroe.com/pac1954-click
Dev board 2: Ideally you have any SHARP Memory Display https://www.adafruit.com/product/3502


Basic description:
- Read out PAC1954 channel 1-3. Channel4 is disabled.
Shunt: 10mR, Vrange: 32V. CH1: Unidirectional. CH2 & 3: Bidirectional. Update rate: 256 SPS.
 
- Display values on Adafruit SHARP Memory Display: CH1...3: Power, Voltage, Current. 

- Send PAC1954 power of channel-1 through BLE, together with battery level in %. 
In the most efficient way for lowest battery consumption. Power level ca. 0dBm.

- Firmware updateability through BLE (With any sample android app).


Detail Awake mode:  
- Read PAC1954: 256 SPS mode avg, Channel 1-3.
- Display on Sharp Memory Display (2Hz update rate) (just basic formatted for development use).
- Optional debug info on UART (for development use).
- Send BLE data (ca. 1Hz): power of PAC1954 CH1, device battery in % (0.1% resolution possible?)
- BLE data send only on request to save power? (Target is mainly Garmin Fenix 7(x), later also Android/ IOS app)
- Able to update firmware through BLE. 
- Total typical power consumption: should be around 1mA average.
Deep sleep: 20min after CH1 & 3 have been below 100mW. 


Detail Deep sleep mode: 
- PAC1954: 8SPS mode, Channel 1 & 3 active only.
- NRF52: deep sleep.
- Total typical power consumption:  few uA. 
Wake up: On button press or PAC1954 power of any channel 1 or 3 ≥ 100mW, PAC alert pins can be used. 


Nic

description:
Hello, 

we are developing a LoRaWAN end node with the STM32WL55JC microcontroller using the mbed OS RTOS. 

The node periodically transmits an uplink packet containing sensor data. After transmission, the node has to go into standby mode to achieve a long battery runtime. 

The rough structure of our firmware is similar to the LoRaWAN example from mbed: https://os.mbed.com/teams/mbed-os-examples/code/mbed-os-example-lorawan/

In our case, the microcontroller remains in an idle state after transmission for a delay of 15min, resulting in high current consumption. 

Your task is to implement a power-saving routine, where the microcontroller changes into standby mode during this wait time. The current consumption should approximately match the 360nA from the datasheet. 

Please contact us if you can implement this standby feature within a few days. We are looking forward to working with you!
title: Low power optimization on STM32: mbed OS and LoRaWAN

description:
We are working with IoT telemetry data and we would like to rework our current unmaintained rules engine.

On average, an IoT unit sends one message per hour, and the data is a simple json containing parameters like: currentBattery, runtimeSinceLastMessage, coordinates, timestamp.

The rules can be configured by the end users in a web UI. Sample rules would be: "Send an email if weekly runtime is lower than 10 hours", "Create an event if the unit left the geofence".

In addition to event-based rules, the rules engine should also support time-based rules which work on asset properties, for example: "Send an email 5 days before leasingEnd".

When implementing the rules engine, we should also think about how to avoid spamming users. For example, a user might have 10 assets where the leasing ends on the same day - in this case we should send a single email with a summary instead of 10 individual emails.

Our stack runs on Google Cloud in GKE. The messages arrive over MQTT and the primary listener is the rules engine which after processing puts messages on a Pub/Sub queue for other consumers.

This would be a greenfield microservice. We imagined it to be a Node.js app written in TypeScript, but we are open to any suggestions, potentially even about solutions involving ready-made components like Prometheus.

We are looking for an expert who can advise and implement a simple and efficient solution.

It is absolutely crucial that you have substantial experience in working with time series data. To show that you are a human, start the message with "Time".
title: Time series expert to set up an IoT rules engine

description:
I'm looking for an expert in a time-series field to help me.

Data.
120 patients.
Data is collected with a frequency of 1000 Hz. Each patient has 5.7556e+06 samples on average, each sample consists of 5 features. 
I resample them by averaging every 45 samples (every 45ms). I tried different rates and this one is an optimal value that produces no significant information loss.
The width of the training window plays a huge role and, as expected, larger window sizes lead to faster convergence at the cost of a higher computation load.
Labels are 13 discrete classes corresponding to the exposure levels at a time step t. 
See the visualization in the attachment.

Classes are imbalanced. I implemented random undersampling to match the number of samples in each class to a specified number of samples. 

Problem setting.
I have trained Transformer and LSTM models.
Models reach good results on the train set, but for some reason don't generalize. The confusion matrix on the train looks basically like an identity matrix, but the validation cm looks random. For the validation, I have completely independent patients.

I think an hour or an hour and a half will suffice to figure it out.
title: Time-series expert to consult on a classification problem.

description:
To generate a 3D point cloud using photogrammetry, we need a suitable algorithm for our iOS iPAD application.

The 3D points are based on the robust recognition of distinctive real corner and crossing points (2D pattern recognition).
The starting point of the pipeline is the SDK function of ARKit (iOS/apple). Here, individual frames with intrinsic and extrinsic camera parameters are made available from the video stream.

The necessary pipeline consists of the following components:

1. ARKit

2. frame

3. Pattern recognition/ 2D feature for prominent corner points

4. Matching of the 2D feature between the individual frame sequences

5. Triangulation and reconstruction of the 3D points between the keyframes

6. local bundle adjustment (Ceres solver) for each individual measurement 

7. Storage of the 3D points of each local single measurement in a common global reference system (octree).

The 3D point cloud is used to overlay or register CAD models with reality (augmented reality). (Not part of the task)

The following skills and experience are beneficial for the project:

- Image Processing ( 2D feature / Descriptor / Matching)
- openCV
-Photogrammetry (Camera model)
- GPU (OpenCL /Metal)
- 3D reconstruction
- Ceres solver BA

A prototype for the pipeline already exists.
The task is to extend and optimize the algorithm.
title: Generation of a 3D point cloud based on photogrammetry
